Throughout life, we all encounter experiences and ideas that make us all question beliefs from our upbringing. For example, in Berton Roueché's book The Medical Detectives, there is an entire section on the placebo effect. The placebo effect that Berton Roueché discussed came from the medical literature where many times during clinical trials the placebo is as effective as the medication that is specifically designed for an ailment.

The idea that pharmaceuticals might not be the full answer was further proven to me from shadowing a doctor at Mount Sinai of Queens hospital. Dr. Butts was working with a diabetic patient who had severe ulcerations of the skin, edema and possibly bone infection from not treating her condition. Dr. Butts told me that most of her problems could be treated with salt water, quitting smoking and taking a walk once a day while wearing shoes. And most importantly, she would never have gotten into that condition if she had done those simple steps.

Over time, these claims and experiences made me want to investigate the role of using the patient’s mind and belief in a treatment to heal his or herself. The Christian Science Religion seemed to be a good starting point to me, because the religion had been in existence since the late 1800’s and I assumed would have a rich library of examples of healing. I began to think that if it were true that it were possible to treat diseases not with drugs, but with changes in people’s thinking and approach to disease, it would alleviate a good deal of problems. And, in addition to solving these problems, this would be done at a relatively low cost with fewer side effects. I began to question then, “Why doesn’t everyone treat disease at some level with this approach?”

As I began to research this topic, I began to encounter aspects that I had not expected. The records of the church were not scientifically documented and nor cataloged for research. There are various lawsuits against the Christian Science Church for child endangerment. Political issues were also discovered because of the federally funded Medicare/Medicaid system paying Christian Science practitioners for non-medical treatment of patients. In addition to these other concerns, there is a controversy with church doctrine in terms of using inappropriate marketing/false advertising to attract new members.

The official name of the church is The First Church of Christ, Scientist. It was founded by Mary Baker Eddy, a woman who had been chronically ill since childhood, in Massachusetts in 1879. In February 1866, after having fallen and suffered internal injuries, her doctors classified her case as terminal. Feeling that she had been abandoned by the medical profession, she began reading her Bible and had a spiritual awakening and according to her own accounts, instantaneous healing. By 1875, she had written her guide to healing via Christian principles and had it published under the name Science and Health.

“What’s the name of that fellow who’s written a book?” asked the sick man, suddenly.

“What book?” enquired the doctor.

“Novel--about the social question--don’t you know? There’s an old chap in it who has money--something like me.”

“Oh! I know. Griggs--that’s the man’s name.”

“What is Griggs, anyway?” asked Robert Lauderdale, in the hoarse growl which served him for a voice at present.

“Griggs? He’s what they call a man of letters, or a literary man, or a novelist, or a genius, or a humbug. I’ve always known him a little, though he’s younger than I am. The only good thing I know about him is that he works hard. Now don’t talk. It isn’t good for you.”

“Well--you talk, then. I’ll listen,” grumbled old Lauderdale.

Thereupon both relapsed into silence, Doctor Routh being one of those people who cannot make conversation to order. Indeed, he was a taciturn man at most times. Lauderdale watched him, coughed a little and turned uneasily, but made a sign to him that he wanted no help.

“Why don’t you talk?” he enquired, at last.

“About Griggs? I haven’t read but one or two of his books. I don’t know what to say about him.”

“Do you think he’s a dangerous friend for a young girl, Routh?”

“Griggs?” Routh laughed in his grey beard. “Hardly! He’s as ugly as a camel, to begin with--and he’s getting on. Griggs--why, Griggs must be fifty, at least. Did you never see him? He’s been about all the spring--came back from the Caucasus in January or February. What put it into your head that he would be a dangerous acquaintance for a young woman?”

“I don’t mean his looks--I mean his ideas.”

“Stuff!” ejaculated Doctor Routh. “He’s only got the modern mania for psychology. What harm can that do?”

“Is that all? Alexander’s an ass.”

Robert Lauderdale turned his head away as though he had settled the question which had tormented him. Again there was a silence in the room. The doctor looked at his patient with a rather inscrutable expression, then took out his watch, replaced it, and consulted his pocket-book. At last he rose and walked toward the window noiselessly on the thick, white carpet.

“I shall have to be going,” he said. “I’ve got a consultation. Cheever’s downstairs.”

Doctor Cheever was Doctor Routh’s assistant, who did not leave the house during Mr. Lauderdale’s illness.

“And you can send away the undertaker, if he’s waiting,” growled the sick man, with an attempt at a laugh. “I say--can I see people, if they call? I suppose my nephews and nieces will be here before long.”

“It’s no use to tell you what to do. You’ll do just what you please, anyway. Professionally, I tell you to keep quiet, not to talk, and to sleep if you can. You’re not like other people,” added Routh, thoughtfully.

“Why not?”

“Most men in your position are badly scared when it comes to going out. The efforts they make to save themselves sometimes kill them. You seem rather indifferent about it. Yet you have a good deal to leave behind you.”

“H’m--I’ve had it all--and a long time. But I want to see Katharine Lauderdale, if she comes.”

“I’ll send for her if it’s anything important,” said Doctor Routh, promptly.

The sick man looked quickly at him. It seemed as though his readiness to send for Katharine implied some doubts as to his patient’s safety.

“I don’t believe I’m going to die,” he said, slowly. “What are my chances, Routh? It’s your duty to tell me, if you know.”

“I don’t know. If I did, I’d tell you. You’re a very sick man--and they’ll all want to see you, of course. I--well, I don’t mean to say anything disagreeable about them. On the contrary--it is natural that they should take an interest--”

Note Referencing Oxford High School Shooting Discovered at Memorial High School in Madison; Arrest Made at La Follette High School for Possession of Stolen Firearm

MADISON, Wis. – In an unsettling turn of events, a note referencing the Oxford High School shooting in Michigan was discovered at Memorial High School in Madison on Thursday afternoon. Principal Matt Hendrickson addressed the school community in an email, assuring parents and students that there is no current security or safety risk.

"I want to inform you of an incident that occurred today at Memorial High School," Hendrickson wrote. "During the school day, a note was discovered in a bathroom. The note referenced the Oxford High School shooting that took place in Michigan last week. I want to assure you that there is no current security or safety risk to our students or staff."

An investigation is underway, with the Madison Police Department and the Central Office of School Safety involved. The note's content and any potential connection to the Oxford High School shooting are currently being examined. The principal urged the school community to remain vigilant and share any concerning information.

"As always, I encourage you to reach out to school administration or school resource officers with any information that could help maintain a safe environment for our students," Hendrickson stated.

On the same day, an 18-year-old student at La Follette High School was arrested for having a loaded gun inside the school. Marquan T. Webb is facing several charges, including possession of a stolen firearm. The loaded gun found with Webb had been reported stolen out of Cottage Grove in September.

Madison Police Department Spokesperson, Marc Lovicott, confirmed the arrest and shared details about the weapon. "The gun was reported stolen in September, and we believe it was brought into the school today," Lovicott said. "There were no injuries reported as a result of the discovery of the note or the arrest."

Hendrickson sent a follow-up email to the Memorial High School community, addressing the arrest and the note. "I wanted to provide you with an update regarding the incidents that occurred today at Memorial and La Follette High Schools," he wrote. "Both incidents are being thoroughly investigated by the Madison Police Department and the Central Office of School Safety. I want to assure you that the safety of our students and staff remains our top priority."

This week, a trend of copycat threats has emerged following the Oxford High School shooting, leading to class cancellations in over a dozen Detroit school districts. The Madison Metropolitan School District and the Madison Police Department are working together to prevent any similar incidents from occurring in Madison.

"The safety of our students and staff is our top priority," Madison Metropolitan School District Spokesperson, Tim Leidner, said. "We are working closely with the Madison Police Department and other law enforcement agencies to ensure a safe learning environment for all students."

Hendrickson ended his email with a message of support and encouragement for the school community. "I want to express my gratitude for the diligence of our staff and students, who reported these incidents, and for the quick response of law enforcement."

As the investigations into the note and the arrest continue, the school community remains on edge. The Madison Metropolitan School District and the Madison Police Department encourage anyone with information to come forward and help maintain a safe environment for all students.

Throughout history, the interactions between the Romans and Germanic tribes were marked by mutual misunderstanding, conflict, and occasional cooperation. A recurring theme in these encounters was the Roman tendency to underestimate the threat posed by Germanic tribes, a miscalculation that often led to significant military setbacks. One such episode unfolded in 113 BC when the Cimbri tribe, driven by a dire need for food and land, crossed into Roman territory. This incursion signaled the beginning of a series of events that challenged Roman dominion in the region.

The confrontation between the Roman forces and the Cimbri tribe in Noricum was a historic turning point. The Cimbri, known for their ferocity and martial prowess, emerged victorious against a Roman army. This triumph marked the first time a Germanic tribe had defeated a Roman military force, unsettling the Roman perception of unchallenged supremacy. Following their success, the Cimbri, alongside the Teutones, continued their offensive, defeating additional Roman armies. This string of victories facilitated a temporary unity among disparate Germanic tribes, driven by a shared goal of resisting Roman expansion.

Germanic tribes, renowned for their warrior culture and eagerness to engage in battle, posed a formidable challenge to Roman hegemony. Despite their shared adversarial stance and periodic alliances, maintaining lasting unity among Germanic tribes remained elusive. Tacitus, in his renowned work "Germania," observed that their "love of liberty" often led to internal strife and prevented cohesive action. This fragmentation presented an opportunity for the Romans, who adeptly exploited tribal divisions to their advantage.

In their diplomatic engagements, the Romans employed strategies that aimed at co-opting tribal leaders. Assimilation was one such tactic, often involving the adoption of Roman customs and practices. Notably, some Germanic children were brought to Rome to be raised within the imperial fold, with the expectation that they would internalize Roman values and influence their tribes upon returning home. This approach was believed to dilute tribal identities and loyalties, thereby facilitating Roman control. However, this strategy was not without its pitfalls.

A prominent example of the backfire of Roman assimilation efforts is Arminius. Educated in Rome, Arminius was expected to become a Roman loyalist and potentially exert influence over his tribe. Instead, Arminius leveraged his Roman training and knowledge against the very empire that sought to mold him. Employing guerrilla tactics, he led a coalition of Germanic tribes in a devastating assault on a Roman legionary force, culminating in the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest in 9 AD. Arminius's actions not only halted Roman expansion into Germanic territories but also elevated him to legendary status among his people, symbolizing resistance to Roman domination. His life and actions underscored the limits of Roman assimilation, illustrating how individual figures could profoundly impact wider historical events.

Stimulus Checks: While Federal Aid Stalls, States Step Up with Relief Payments and Bonuses

As the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic continues to be felt across the nation, many Americans are looking to their elected officials for financial relief. However, a fourth federal stimulus check, as evidenced by a petition with over 2.9 million signatures requesting $2,000 recurring payments, is unlikely to materialize in the near future.

Jen Psaki, White House Press Secretary, addressed the possibility of additional federal stimulus checks during a press briefing, stating, "The President strongly believes that the American Rescue Plan is the most effective tool to address the crisis at this moment, and his focus is on getting this relief to the American people as quickly as possible."

Despite the lack of federal action, several state governments have taken matters into their own hands to provide additional financial relief. In California, for instance, millions of residents are receiving a second Golden State Stimulus check, with payments ranging from $600 to $1,100. This initiative aims to support low-income residents who have been impacted by the pandemic.

In Maryland, low-income individuals and families are eligible for direct payments of $300 or $500. Additionally, educators in states like Florida, Michigan, and Tennessee have received bonuses to help offset the challenges they have faced during the pandemic.

Advance monthly child tax credit payments of up to $300 per child have continued through December as part of the American Rescue Plan. Discussions surrounding future aid packages in federal budget proposals have also included the possibility of extending these payments. Families qualifying for the expanded child tax credit can receive up to $3,600 per child, with the option to receive these payments monthly or in a lump sum.

Meanwhile, third stimulus payments of up to $1,400 are still being distributed. These payments include 'plus-up' payments for individuals who have experienced income changes since filing their taxes and provisions for new dependents in 2021.

California's Golden State Stimulus I and II are also targeted at supporting low-income residents, with one-time payments of $600 or $1,100 being distributed. Maryland has issued payments to individuals and families claiming the earned income tax credit and provided additional support for the unemployed and small businesses.

Front-line workers in Vermont have received hazard pay for their early pandemic work, and educators in several states have received bonus payments to help offset the challenges they have faced during the pandemic.

While the first three stimulus checks have gone a long way in reducing financial hardships for many Americans, current federal proposals do not include further direct payments. As the economy continues to recover, the importance of state and local relief efforts becomes increasingly apparent.

"Rittenhouse Verdict: A Tragic Reminder of the Dangers of Unchecked Gun Culture"

In the wake of Kyle Rittenhouse's acquittal for shooting three men during a Kenosha riot, including two unarmed individuals, many are left reeling at the blatant injustice of it all. While Rittenhouse has been hailed as a hero by some, including Donald Trump, the reality is far more disturbing. The jury's decision to acquit Rittenhouse highlights the flaws in our current interpretation of self-defense laws, affording too much power to armed individuals in determining who poses a threat.

The comparison between Rittenhouse's case and the trial of Ahmaud Arbery's killers is particularly telling. In both instances, the perpetrators claimed self-defense, but the outcomes could not have been more different. While the Arbery killers were held accountable for their actions, Rittenhouse was given a free pass. This inconsistency underscores the need for stricter gun control laws and a reevaluation of our self-defense laws.

Rittenhouse's decision not to provide medical assistance or immediately contact the police after shooting Rosenbaum is particularly scrutinized. In a moment of chaos and violence, it is unconscionable that Rittenhouse would prioritize his own safety over the well-being of his victims. This callous disregard for human life is a stark reminder of the dangers of armed individuals roaming our streets.

The actions of Anthony Huber, who attempted to disarm Rittenhouse and was then killed, are a testament to courage in the face of overwhelming danger. Huber's selfless act of trying to protect others is a stark contrast to Rittenhouse's quickness to use his gun. The jury's decision to acquit Rittenhouse only serves to embolden such dangerous behavior, leading to more armed confrontations at public events.

The incident involving Gaige Grosskreutz, who Rittenhouse wounded, is another example of the dangers of unchecked gun culture. Grosskreutz was simply trying to de-escalate the situation when he was shot by Rittenhouse. This senseless violence could have been avoided if Rittenhouse had not been so quick to use his gun.

The Rittenhouse verdict is a tragic reminder of the need for stricter gun control laws and a reevaluation of our self-defense laws. It is imperative that we take action to prevent future tragedies similar to the Kenosha shooting. The safety of our communities depends on it.

In conclusion, the acquittal of Kyle Rittenhouse is a sobering reminder of the dangers of unchecked gun culture. The jury's decision to afford too much power to armed individuals in determining who poses a threat is a recipe for disaster. It is time for us to take action and demand stricter gun control laws and a reevaluation of our self-defense laws. The safety of our communities depends on it.

As dawn broke with a passion of golden light, Cass found himself again in the same eerie glen where the previous day's horrors had unfolded. This time, however, he was not alone. The girl, whose name he learned was Seraphine, was there before him, a figure of striking resilience in the face of the morning's pallor.

"You're back," she greeted him with a voice that, despite the grim circumstances, carried an undertone of gratitude. "I was half afraid you'd taken my suggestion to heart and gone for help."

Cass shook his head, suppressing the urge to find comfort in her presence. "No. It's... it's too early to leave a mystery like this unsolved."

Seraphine nodded, her eyes alight with that same peculiar curiosity. "A mystery indeed. I've been thinking, Cass. What if we were to investigate a bit further? I've found something... peculiar. Over there!" she pointed to a spot behind a cluster of trees.

As they approached, Cass could see what had captured her interest: a small, charred object partially buried in the earth. It was a cigarette case, its ornate silver frame tarnished, but still recognizable in its craftsmanship.

"A gentleman's accessory," Seraphine mused, "in a place so far from civilization. Perhaps he was courting danger in more ways than one."

Cass frowned, the notion sending a shiver down his spine. "This man... he must have been in danger. Look at this." He pointed to the bullet hole in the dead man's hat, now clearly visible against the pale morning sky.

Seraphine leaned in, her eyes narrowing as she examined the hat, the bullet wound, and then the body. "He's been well-dressed, but look at the state of him. It's as if there's a deliberate contrast. His clothes, so fine, and..." Her voice trailed off as she looked at the stain on the ground, a dark mark that spelled out the grim truth.

Cass nodded, his thoughts racing. "It's as if the killer took this man as he was, in all his finery, and... and made him less than human."

Seraphine's eyes, already bright with curiosity, sparkled with a determination that was both unsettling and captivating. "Then we must find out who he was. And why. This isn't just a murder, Cass. It's a statement. A message, left for us to decipher."

Cass felt a grim respect for her resolve. "You're right. We cannot leave this to chance. We must find answers."

"Then we shall," Seraphine declared, her voice ringing with an almost reckless enthusiasm. "We'll start by unraveling this mystery. We'll find out who this man was, why he met his end here, and we'll make sure his killer does not go unpunished."

Together, Cass and Seraphine stood before the stark tableau of death and mystery, united in their quest for truth in the face of the unknown. Their footsteps crunched the brittle leaves of the forest as they ventured deeper, guided by an unseen force, driven by a shared resolve to confront the shadows lurking in the heart of the glen.

Their journey would take them through the tangled web of the forest, each twist and turn leading them closer to the truth, yet further from the safety of the known world. They would encounter allies and foes, each with their own secrets and motives. But through it all, their bond would grow, strengthened by the shared experience of fear and the relentless pursuit of justice.

And as the sun dipped below the horizon, painting the sky in hues of crimson and gold, Cass and Seraphine knew they had only begun their odyssey. The mysteries that lay ahead were vast and perilous, but together, they were prepared to face them, come what may.

Harris Slams Trump's 'Abuse of Power' in Georgia Election Interference

Vice President-elect Kamala Harris criticized President Donald Trump for his recent phone call to Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger, in which he urged the official to overturn the state's election results. Harris described the call as a "bald-faced, bold abuse of power" during a drive-thru rally in Savannah, Georgia.

The recorded conversation between Trump and Raffensperger was obtained by CNN and reported by the Washington Post. Senior adviser to President-elect Joe Biden, Bob Bauer, called the call a "disgraceful story about Donald Trump’s assault on American democracy."

Harris highlighted the failed attempts by Trump and other Republicans to overturn the election results on baseless voter fraud allegations. "The president's efforts to undermine the integrity of our democracy are a threat to our nation's very foundation," she said.

Harris emphasized Georgia's role in electing Biden and herself, criticizing the opposition's questioning of the electoral process. "The people of Georgia have spoken, and their voices must be heard," she said. "It's time for the president and his allies to respect the will of the people and accept the results of this election."

Trump's January 2 audio call with Raffensperger, along with White House chief of staff Mark Meadows and several lawyers, was leaked and reported. In the call, Trump pressured Raffensperger to "find" enough votes to overturn Biden's victory in Georgia.

Harris condemned Trump's claims that the January 5 Senate runoff elections were "illegal and invalid." "These baseless allegations are a desperate attempt to undermine the democratic process and discredit the will of the people," she said.

Harris, addressing future representation, expressed concern over the absence of a Black woman in the Senate after her resignation. "It's crucial that we continue to have diverse representation in our government, especially in the Senate," she said. "We must ensure that the voices of all Americans are heard and represented."

Senate candidate Jon Ossoff accused Trump of attempting to disenfranchise Black voters and criticized Sens. Perdue and Loeffler for not defending Georgia voters. "It's unconscionable that the president would try to silence the voices of Black voters in Georgia," he said. "We must stand up against these attacks on our democracy and ensure that every voice is heard."

Harris's comments come as Trump continues to face backlash for his attempts to overturn the election results. The president's actions have been widely criticized by Democrats and some Republicans, who argue that he is undermining the integrity of the democratic process.

In a statement, Bauer called Trump's actions "a direct attack on the rule of law and the principles of democracy." He added, "The president's efforts to manipulate the election results are a threat to our nation's very foundation."

Harris's remarks also highlight the ongoing battle for representation in the Senate. The vice president-elect has been a vocal advocate for diversity and inclusion in government, and her comments on the importance of Black representation in the Senate reflect her commitment to ensuring that all voices are heard.

As the nation continues to grapple with the fallout of the 2020 election, Harris's words serve as a reminder of the importance of protecting our democracy and ensuring that every voice is heard. The vice president-elect's leadership and commitment to diversity and inclusion are a beacon of hope for a brighter, more equitable future.

Tiger Woods Rushed to Surgery After Devastating Los Angeles Car Crash

Golf legend Tiger Woods underwent emergency surgery following a severe car crash in Los Angeles County early Tuesday morning, which left him with serious leg injuries. The crash occurred around 7 a.m., and Woods, while conscious, was found trapped in his wrecked SUV when first responders arrived at the scene.

Los Angeles County Sheriff's Deputy Carlos Gonzalez was among the first to respond and offered his insights during a press briefing. "When I arrived at the scene, Mr. Woods was lucid and calm; he identified himself as 'Tiger'," Gonzalez recounted, emphasizing the speed with which they acted to free him from the damaged vehicle.

Fire Chief Daryl Osby confirmed the complexities faced during the rescue. "We utilized the 'jaws of life' to extricate Mr. Woods from the vehicle. Given the nature of the accident, it's a miracle he survived."

According to the Los Angeles Times, Woods sustained significant injuries, including a shattered ankle and two leg fractures, one of which was deemed a compound fracture. Mark Steinberg, Woods' longtime manager, conveyed the gravity of the situation in a statement, saying, "Tiger is currently in surgery, and we appreciate your privacy and support."

The accident involved Woods' SUV hitting a center divider and experiencing multiple rollovers, as reported by Sheriff Alex Villanueva. "The vehicle was traveling at a greater speed than normal," Villanueva explained, indicating that the primary cause seemed to be excessive speed. However, he clarified that there was no evidence suggesting Woods was impaired or under the influence at the time of the crash.

The day preceding the accident, Woods had spent time at the Rolling Hills Country Club in the company of former NBA star Dwyane Wade. Reports also surfaced regarding Woods appearing agitated before the crash, though further details remain unclear.

The crash comes on the heels of Woods' fifth back surgery in December, which had already cast doubt on his participation in the upcoming 2021 Masters Tournament. In 2019, Woods made a historic comeback by winning The Masters, securing his 15th major championship victory, a moment celebrated by fans and peers alike.

PGA Tour Commissioner Jay Monahan spoke about the impact of the news on the golf community. "Tiger is a true fighter, both on and off the course. We are all pulling for him and wish him a swift recovery."

Support for Woods has poured in from across the sports world. Former Olympic skier Lindsey Vonn tweeted her concern, saying, "Praying for TW right now," while golf legends Jack Nicklaus and Justin Thomas have expressed their hope and support for Woods' recovery.

"Whenever we have an accident like this, our first thought is about the safety and recovery of those involved," Sheriff Villanueva added, highlighting the hope shared by many fans and fellow athletes for Woods’ swift comeback.

As Woods remains in the hospital, the investigation into the crash continues, focusing on the vehicle's speed at the time of the accident. Meanwhile, his family, fans, and the entire golf community await updates on his condition and recovery.

Historic Second Impeachment of Trump: House Round Delivers Unprecedented Bipartisan Support

CNN – In a momentous and historic decision, the House of Representatives voted to impeach President Donald Trump for a second time, marking an unprecedented level of bipartisan support with 10 Republicans joining Democrats in the effort. This impeachment vote is noted for its record-breaking nature, having become the most bipartisan impeachment in the history of the United States.

Though 10 Republican representatives crossed party lines to support impeachment, a significant 197 Republicans voted against it, underscoring the extent of division and partisanship that continues to characterize American politics. This event amplifies the already high level of polarization seen in Washington and distinguishes from past impeachments that largely adhered to party lines.

In contrast to this most recent vote, previous impeachments — including those of Andrew Johnson, Bill Clinton, and the first impeachment of Donald Trump — saw little to no crossover support from the opposing party. The departure of even a small group of Republicans from their party’s steadfast support of Trump is thus noteworthy.

Among the Republicans who voted in favor were several influential figures. Notable among them were Rep. Liz Cheney of Wyoming, the third-highest-ranking House Republican, and Rep. Tom Rice of South Carolina. Neither Cheney nor Rice are widely regarded as moderates, yet their decision to support impeachment reflects mounting concerns within some GOP ranks regarding Trump's conduct.

The decision by those 10 Republicans comes amidst reports indicating a decline in Trump's job approval rating among Republican voters, though it remains robust at over 70%. This sustained approval illustrates Trump's enduring influence over a considerable portion of the Republican base despite the current backlash.

Two of the Republicans who voted for impeachment hail from Washington state, which uses a top-two primary system. This political mechanism may have influenced their decision-making, as such a system tends to allow more moderate and independent-minded candidates to advance in elections.

This modern impeachment has only one historical parallel with significant Republican support - the impeachment threat faced by President Richard Nixon in 1974. Nixon ultimately resigned before an impeachment vote could be held, but he had already lost the backing of many in his own party, an uncommon scenario in historical contexts.

Highlighting their solidarity, no Democrats voted against impeaching Trump, marking a record level of unity within the party at this critical juncture. This degree of cohesion is particularly significant given the occasional rifts observed in recent years over various policy issues.

It is essential to note, however, that impeachment in the House is merely the first step in the process and does not in itself remove a president from office. The Senate now faces its own test, with its reaction to the impeachment vote uncertain and pivotal to the next steps.

Whether or not the Senate will join the House in a bipartisan manner remains an unresolved question. The Senate's decision is crucial in determining whether Trump will be convicted and potentially barred from holding future office.

The consistency of Trump's support within the GOP, despite his second impeachment, highlights the complex dynamics within the party. While in recent history party lines are only rarely crossed, today's political climate shows an inclination towards fragmentation among traditional Republican ranks.

The political implications of this impeachment, coupled with the actions in the Senate, have the capacity to reshape political alliances and influence the trajectory of the Republican Party for years to come.

As the nation awaits the Senate's next move, the unfolding events continue to draw the attention of both domestic and international observers. The outcome will likely have a profound impact on the political landscape and will be studied as a pivotal moment in American political history for many years to come.

This historic second impeachment not only highlights partisan divisions but also points to shifting allegiances and growing unrest within political parties grappling with extraordinary circumstances. How these dynamics play out could shape the future of American governance in unpredictable ways.

In the 19th century, the Afro-Portuguese exerted significant influence in central Angola, dominating semi-autonomous kingdoms that bordered coastal ports. These mestiço communities, though technically under Portuguese sovereignty, operated with a degree of local autonomy governed by prominent mestiço families. Despite their mixed European and African heritage, the Afro-Portuguese consciously distanced themselves from indigenous African populations, viewing themselves as a distinct entity due to their unique socio-cultural and economic status.

As the 19th century progressed into the early 20th, a socio-cultural transformation unfolded, as Afro-Portuguese families integrated with Kimbundu-speaking groups, leading to the formation of the modern Mbundu ethnic identity. This transition was marked by intermarriage and cultural assimilation, reshaping the sociopolitical landscape of the region. The historical dominance of the Afro-Portuguese, however, had sown the seeds of division between the coastal inhabitants and the inland communities, contributing to the complex social fabric that would later influence post-colonial conflicts.

The late 1800s saw increased external pressure from British and German colonial ambitions, which compelled the Portuguese to reassess their colonial strategies. In response to these pressures, direct Portuguese control became the norm, supplanting the previous system of indirect rule. This shift significantly affected the economic prowess of the Afro-Portuguese, particularly those engaged in the lucrative caravan trade across the interior. The advent of modern transportation technology further eroded their economic influence, altering the dynamics of commerce and power within the region.

Simultaneously, the Portuguese implemented a colonial assimilation policy to delineate social hierarchy, distinguishing between indígena and assimilado populations. Assimilados, which comprised established Afro-Portuguese families and Africans educated by missionaries, were granted certain political rights and citizenship. This categorization was contingent upon meeting specific cultural and educational criteria, reflecting the colonial state's attempt to create a stratified society. The assimilation policy, while ostensibly promoting integration, ultimately reinforced divisions and highlighted the enduring legacy of the Afro-Portuguese era on the evolving political and cultural identity of Angola.

Judge Bars Rittenhouse from Associating with White Supremacists Following Bail Violation

KENOSHA, Wis. (AP) – A Wisconsin judge has ruled that Kyle Rittenhouse, facing multiple charges for fatally shooting two people during protests in Kenosha, must not associate with known white supremacist groups, following an incident where he was seen fraternizing with their members at a local bar.

Rittenhouse, who was just 17 at the time of the incident, is charged with reckless and intentional homicide, endangerment, and being a minor in possession of a firearm. The shootings occurred amid protests triggered by the police shooting of Jacob Blake, a Black man, last August. The high-profile case has seen Rittenhouse pleading not guilty to all charges, maintaining he acted in self-defense.

Prosecutors have alleged that Rittenhouse traveled from his home in Illinois to Kenosha, Wisconsin, with the intent of joining militia groups that claimed to be safeguarding businesses during the unrest. These allegations were further fueled by recent reports that within hours after his release on bail, he was seen at a Wisconsin bar drinking beer and taking photos while making a hand gesture commonly associated with white supremacist groups.

In light of these developments, the judge modified Rittenhouse's bail conditions. Under the new terms, Rittenhouse is strictly prohibited from associating with individuals or groups known to harass others based on race, religion, color, national origin, or gender. Additionally, the conditions forbid him from possessing firearms and consuming alcohol, a move prosecutors argued was necessary following his interaction with individuals tied to white supremacist beliefs.

This legal development followed a visit to a local tavern where Rittenhouse, now 18, was photographed with men thought to be members of the Proud Boys, a far-right group known for violent confrontations. During the visit, he was also caught on video singing a song considered an anthem among several right-leaning groups, prompting the prosecutors to seek stricter bail terms.

Rittenhouse's case has become a flashpoint in broader national debates over gun rights, self-defense laws, and the racial dimensions of policing and protest. His situation has garnered significant attention, with many conservative figures and media personalities rallying in his defense, portraying him as a patriot retaliating against lawlessness.

As the legal proceedings continue, Rittenhouse remains free on a $2 million bond, largely funded through donations from his supporters. His trial is slated to advance under intense public scrutiny, with implications that might resonate far beyond the court's walls.

In examining the epic narrative of "Beowulf," one finds a compelling exploration of individual combat and the courage it demands in the face of formidable opponents. Beowulf’s battles are decidedly personal, emphasizing the hero's solitary struggle against threats that not only test physical strength but also the very fabric of his character. His encounters with Grendel, Grendel's mother, and ultimately the dragon, provide a rich tapestry through which individual valor and existential themes intertwine. Critics such as J.R.R. Tolkien highlight the contrast between Beowulf's youthful audacity and his somber final moments, asserting that this duality encapsulates the essence of heroism—a journey marked by the evolution of both personal resolve and societal expectations.

In his initial confrontation with Grendel, Beowulf consciously fights unarmed, eschewing weapons to manifest a profound sense of fairness and faith in divine providence. This act underscores Beowulf’s belief in a predestined outcome, where valor dictated his tactics. As his hands grapple with the ferocious beast, the absence of traditional arms paradoxically amplifies his inherent strength and courage. The heroic ethos conveyed here parallels age-old traditions found in mythological narratives, evoking the image of a hero who relies on personal integrity over mere weaponry. This idea is echoed in as Beowulf declares, “Fate will unwind as it must,” suggesting that the course of battle is inextricably tied to one's inherent qualities rather than external advantages.

As the narrative progresses, the challenges Beowulf faces grow more formidable. The confrontation with Grendel's mother requires an ancient sword, illustrating not only Beowulf's extraordinary physical prowess but also the shifting nature of conflict he encounters. The massive sword symbolizes a confluence of ancient strength and modern warfare, emphasizing a departure in tactics as Beowulf transitions from a reliance on personal valor to the acceptance of historical armaments. Yet, even here, his victory is not merely a result of the weapon’s might but of his fortified spirit and unwavering faith—qualities that transcend the physical tool of battle. Tolkien's interpretation suggests a melancholic realization that, with age and experience, the hero learns that even the mightiest can face insurmountable odds, and it is often the internal struggles that continue long after the visible battles have ended.

In contrast to the singular and often personal nature of his early combat, Beowulf's final confrontation with the dragon reveals the evolution of warfare itself—one that requires conventional weapons amidst the uncanny. This shift in tactics signifies a philosophical commentary on the nature of true strength and the complexities of existence. The dragon, representing an ultimate foe, stands not only as a physical opponent but as a metaphorical embodiment of Beowulf’s inner demons; the solitude he experiences in this battle underscores his existential loneliness. The epic thus reflects the notion that, in life, the fiercest battles are often those fought within one’s psyche, a theme prevalent in mythological narratives worldwide. The hero, standing alone against such profound threats, embodies "Northern courage," a theme that resonates through action rather than grandiloquent speech—an idea echoed in the simple yet powerful assertion that "actions speak louder than words."

In conclusion, "Beowulf" intricately interweaves individual courage, existential struggle, and the essence of true strength. It posits that while external weapons may fail against supernatural forces, the innermost convictions—the faith in one’s purpose and the courage to confront one’s demons—serve as one’s true arsenal. The narrative’s enduring legacy lies in its capacity to portray the hero not merely as a wielder of swords, but as a figure whose greatest battles are those that are internal, echoing the timeless message of mythic tales across cultures that valor transcends the material. In the end, Beowulf’s hands and heart, forged through faith and fortitude in the face of life’s ultimate challenges, emerge as his greatest weapons, illuminating the complex interplay between heroism and humanity in the grand tapestry of existence.

"Ah, well, the Prince is married," cried Fritz, with a coarse burst of laughter.

"That seems to entertain you, sir," said Otto.

"Ay," said the young boor. "Did you not know that? I thought all Europe knew it!" And he added a pantomime of a nature to explain his accusation to the dullest.

"Ah sir," said Mr. Gottesheim, "it is very plain that you are not from hereabouts! But the truth is, that the whole princely family and Court are rips and rascals, not one to mend another. They live, sir, in idleness and--what most commonly follows it--corruption. The Princess has a lover; a Baron, as he calls himself, from East Prussia; and the Prince is so little of a man, sir, that he holds the candle. Nor is that the worst of it, for this foreigner and his paramour are suffered to transact the state affairs, while the Prince takes the salary and leaves all things to go to wrack. There will follow upon this some manifest judgment which, though I am old, I may survive to see."

"Good man, you are in the wrong about Gondremark," said Fritz, showing a greatly increased animation; "but for all the rest, you speak the God's truth like a good patriot. As for the Prince, if he would take and strangle his wife, I would forgive him yet."

"Nay, Fritz," said the old man, "that would be to add iniquity to evil. For you perceive, sir," he continued, once more addressing himself to the unfortunate Prince, "this Otto has himself to thank for these disorders. He has his young wife, and his principality, and he has sworn to cherish both."

"Sworn at the altar!" echoed Fritz. "But put your faith in princes!"

"Well, sir, he leaves them both to an adventurer from East Prussia," pursued the farmer: "leaves the girl to be seduced and to go on from bad to worse, till her name's become a tap-room by-word, and she not yet twenty; leaves the country to be overtaxed, and bullied with armaments, and jockied into war----"

"War!" cried Otto.

"So they say, sir; those that watch their ongoings, say to war," asseverated Killian. "Well, sir, that is very sad; it is a sad thing for this poor, wicked girl to go down to hell with people's curses; it's a sad thing for a tight little happy country to be misconducted; but whoever may complain, I humbly conceive, sir, that this Otto cannot. What he has worked for, that he has got; and may God have pity on his soul, for a great and a silly sinner's!"

"He has broke his oath; then he is a perjurer. He takes the money and leaves the work; why, then plainly he's a thief. A cuckold he was before, and a fool by birth. Better me that!" cried Fritz, and snapped his fingers.

"And now, sir, you will see a little," continued the farmer, "why we think so poorly of this Prince Otto. There's such a thing as a man being pious and honest in the private way; and there is such a thing, sir, as a public virtue; but when a man has neither, the Lord lighten him! Even this Gondremark, that Fritz here thinks so much of----"

"Ay," interrupted Fritz, "Gondremark's the man for me. I would we had his like in Gerolstein."

"He is a bad man," said the old farmer, shaking his head; "and there was never good begun by the breach of God's commandments. But so far I will go with you: he is a man that works for what he has."

"I tell you he's the hope of Grünewald," cried Fritz. "He doesn't suit some of your high-and-dry, old, ancient ideas; but he's a downright modern man--a man of the new lights and the progress of the age. He does some things wrong; so they all do; but he has the people's interests next his heart; and you mark me--you, sir, who are a Liberal, and the enemy of all their governments, you please to mark my words--the day will come in Grünewald, when they take out that yellow-headed skulk of a Prince and that dough-faced Messalina of a Princess, march 'em back foremost over the borders, and proclaim the Baron Gondremark first President. I've heard them say it in a speech. I was at a meeting once at Brandenau, and the Mittwalden delegates spoke up for fifteen thousand. Fifteen thousand, all brigaded, and each man with a medal round his neck to rally by. That's all Gondremark."

The old man had been made sullen and angry enough by the unauthorized disappearance of his son with the new purchase; but when he saw the empty saddle and disabled condition of the lamed animal, a sudden panic seized upon him. He hurried into the house with strange pallor on his sunburned face and a tremor of the knees, which made him glad to drop into a chair when he reached the kitchen, where his wife was moving about her work with the same feverish restlessness that had ended so painfully with him.

The woman, startled by his appearance, came up to him in subdued agitation.

"It is only that the new beast has come home lamed, and with the saddle empty," he said, in reply to her look. "I must go to the village, or find some of the grooms. Keep up a good heart, dame, till I come back."

"Is he hurt? Oh, John! is there any sign that our lad has come to harm?" questioned the poor woman, shaking from head to foot, as she supported herself by the back of the chair from which her husband started in haste to be off.

"I will soon know--I will soon know"--was his answer. "God help us!"

"God help us!" repeated the woman, dropping helplessly down into the chair, as her husband put on his hat and went hurriedly through the door; and there she sat trembling until another sound of pain, that seemed mournfully human, reached her from the stable-yard.

This appeal to her compassion divided somewhat the agony of her fears, and strengthened her for kindly exertion. "Poor beast," she thought, "no one is taking care of him."

She looked around; no aid was near. The tired farm-hands had gone to bed, or wandered off to the village. She was rather glad of that. It was something that she could appease her own anxiety by giving help to anything in distress. Taking up the lantern, which was still alight, she went toward the stable, and there limping out of the darkness met the wounded horse. An active housewife like Mrs. Storms required no help in relieving the animal of its trappings. She unbuckled the girth, took off the saddle, and passed her hand gently down the fore leg, that shrunk and quivered even under that slight touch.

"It is a sprain, and a bad one," she thought, leading the poor beast into his stall, where he lay down wearily; "but no bones are broken. Oh, if he could only speak now and tell me if my lad is alive--or--or--Oh, my God, have mercy upon me, have mercy upon me!"

Here the poor woman leaned her shoulder against the side of the stall, and a burning moisture broke into her eyes, filling them with pain; for this woman was given to endurance, and, with such, weeping is seldom a relief; but looking downward at the pathetic and almost human appeal in the great wild eyes of the wounded horse, tears partaking of compassion as well as grief swelled into drops and ran down her face in comforting abundance. So, patting the poor beast on his soiled neck, she went to the house again and heating some decoction of leaves that she gathered from under the garden wall, came back with her lantern and bathed the swollen limb until the horse laid his head upon the straw, and bore the slackened pain with patience.

It was a pity that some other work of mercy did not present itself to assuage the suspense that was becoming almost unendurable to a woman waiting to know of the life or death of her only son. She could not sit down in her accustomed place and wait, but turned from the threshold heart-sick, and, still holding the lantern, wandered up and down a lane that ran half a mile before it reached the highway--up and down until it seemed to her as if unnumbered hours had passed since she had seen her husband go forth to learn whether she was a childless mother or not. "Would he never come?"

"I should have gone to the wall," he thought, "but a young fellow from the Didots will pull through."

The septuagenarian sighed for the time when he could live at ease in his own fashion. If his knowledge of the higher branches of the craft of printing was scanty, on the other hand, he was supposed to be past master of an art which workmen pleasantly call "tipple-ography," an art held in high esteem by the divine author of Pantagruel; though of late, by reason of the persecution of societies yclept of Temperance, the cult has fallen, day by day, into disuse.

Jerome-Nicolas Sechard, bound by the laws of etymology to be a dry subject, suffered from an inextinguishable thirst. His wife, during her lifetime, managed to control within reasonable bounds the passion for the juice of the grape, a taste so natural to the bear that M. de Chateaubriand remarked it among the ursine tribes of the New World. But philosophers inform us that old age is apt to revert to the habits of youth, and Sechard senior is a case in poin–he older he grew, the better he loved to drink. The master-passion had given a stamp of originality to an ursine physiognomy; his nose had developed till it reached the proportions of a double great-canon A; his veined cheeks looked like vine-leaves, covered, as they were, with bloated patches of purple, madder red, and often mottled hues; till altogether, the countenance suggested a huge truffle clasped about by autumn vine tendrils. The little gray eyes, peering out from beneath thick eyebrows like bushes covered with snow, were agleam with the cunning of avarice that had extinguished everything else in the man, down to the very instinct of fatherhood. Those eyes never lost their cunning even when disguised in drink. Sechard put you in mind of one of La Fontaine's Franciscan friars, with the fringe of grizzled hair still curling about his bald pate. He was short and corpulent, like one of the old-fashioned lamps for illumination, that burn a vast deal of oil to a very small piece of wick; for excess of any sort confirms the habit of body, and drunkenness, like much study, makes the fat man stouter, and the lean man leaner still.

For thirty years Jerome-Nicolas-Sechard had worn the famous municipal three-cornered hat, which you may still see here and there on the head of the towncrier in out-of-the-way places. His breeches and waistcoat were of greenish velveteen, and he wore an old-fashioned brown greatcoat, gray cotton stockings, and shoes with silver buckles to them. This costume, in which the workman shone through the burgess, was so thoroughly in keeping with the man's character, defects, and way of life, that he might have come ready dressed into the world. You could no more imagine him apart from his clothes than you could think of a bulb without its husk. If the old printer had not long since given the measure of his blind greed, the very nature of the man came out in the manner of his abdication.

Knowing, as he did, that his son must have learned his business pretty thoroughly in the great school of the Didots, he had yet been ruminating for a long while over the bargain that he meant to drive with David. All that the father made, the son, of course, was bound to lose, but in business this worthy knew nothing of father or son. If, in the first instance, he had looked on David as his only child, later he came to regard him as the natural purchaser of the business, whose interests were therefore his own. Sechard meant to sell dear; David, of course, to buy cheap; his son, therefore, was an antagonist, and it was his duty to get the better of him. The transformation of sentiment into self-seeking, ordinarily slow, tortuous, and veiled by hypocrisy in better educated people, was swift and direct in the old "bear," who demonstrated the superiority of shrewd tipple-ography over book-learned typography.

As the last notes of the echoed song faded away, a solemn silence fell upon the landscape, like a veil of mystery gently cast over the rugged terrain. The baron, still shaken by the sudden interruption, grasped the reins of Mistraon with a firmer hand, his eyes scanning the surrounding hills as if in search of the elusive voice that had mirrored Reine des Anbiez's melody.

The young girl, oblivious to the brief moment of peril, continued on her way, her feet carrying her towards a nearby clearing, where a babbling brook sang its own gentle song. The baron, still recovering from his surprise, followed her at a distance, his gaze fixed upon the gentle sway of her movements, as if mesmerized by the rhythmic flow of her steps.

Erebus, now walking beside the baron, seemed to sense his master's distraction, and with a soft whine, nudged his hand, as if to rouse him from his reverie. The baron, startled, looked down at the faithful hound, and smiled, his thoughts returning to the present moment. Together, they followed Reine des Anbiez, who had now reached the edge of the clearing, and was gazing out at the breathtaking vista before her.

The sun, now beginning its descent towards the horizon, cast a warm orange glow over the landscape, illuminating the rolling hills and the dark green forests that stretched towards the distant mountains. A gentle breeze rustled the leaves of the trees, creating a soft murmur that filled the air, like the whispered secrets of the forest. Reine des Anbiez, entranced by the beauty of the scene, stood motionless, her eyes drinking in the splendor of the view.

As the baron and Erebus approached, they too were struck by the majesty of the landscape, and for a moment, the three stood there, frozen in awe, the only sound the soft rustling of the leaves and the distant song of the brook. The air was filled with an almost palpable sense of peace, as if the very essence of the natural world had been distilled into this one perfect moment.

Reine des Anbiez, breaking the spell, turned to the baron, a smile playing on her lips, and said, "Is it not beautiful, dear baron? Does it not fill your heart with joy and wonder?" The baron, still under the enchantment of the moment, nodded, his eyes never leaving the view, and replied, "It is indeed breathtaking, my dear. A true masterpiece of nature's artistry."

Erebus, as if sensing the baron's distraction, lay down at his feet, his eyes fixed upon Reine des Anbiez, as if guarding her from some unseen danger. The young girl, noticing the hound's intense gaze, laughed, and said, "Fear not, dear Erebus, I am safe, and the baron's attention is merely captured by the beauty of the view." Erebus, seeming to understand, relaxed, his tail thumping gently against the ground.

As the sun continued its descent, the colors of the sky deepened, and the stars began to twinkle like diamonds in the darkening blue. Reine des Anbiez, shivering slightly, drew her cloak around her, and turned to the baron, saying, "Shall we return to the chateau, dear baron? The evening air grows cool, and I fear my betrothed may be waiting for us."

The baron, reluctant to break the spell of the moment, hesitated, but eventually nodded, and together they began their descent from the hill, Erebus walking faithfully beside them. As they walked, the darkness deepened, and the only sound was the soft crunch of gravel beneath their feet, and the distant hooting of an owl, echoing through the forest like a mournful sigh.

The chateau, nestled in the valley below, shone like a beacon, its windows glowing with a warm, golden light, like the welcoming smile of a loved one. Reine des Anbiez, quickening her pace, seemed eager to return to the warmth and comfort of the chateau, and the baron, sensing her eagerness, matched his steps to hers, Erebus trotting faithfully beside them.

As they approached the chateau, the sound of laughter and music drifted through the air, and Reine des Anbiez's face lit up with excitement, "It seems we have arrived just in time for dinner, dear baron. My betrothed must have arranged a surprise for us." The baron, smiling, offered her his arm, and together they entered the chateau, Erebus following closely behind.

The warm glow of the fire pit, and the soft murmur of conversation, enveloped them, like a gentle embrace, and Reine des Anbiez, smiling, was swept up in the greetings of her betrothed and the other guests. The baron, watching her, felt a pang of melancholy, as if he were witnessing a scene from a life that was not his own.

Erebus, sensing his master's mood, nuzzled his hand, and the baron, smiling, scratched the hound behind the ears, his thoughts returning to the present moment. The music, and the laughter, and the warm glow of the fire, all combined to create a sense of conviviality, and the baron, shedding his melancholy, joined in the conversation, his spirits lifted by the warmth and camaraderie of the gathering.

As the evening wore on, and the night deepened, the baron found himself drawn into the joy and laughter of the party, his earlier concerns and doubts forgotten in the face of the warmth and hospitality of the chateau. Reine des Anbiez, radiant and happy, shone like a star, her beauty and charm captivating all who surrounded her, and the baron, watching her, felt his heart fill with a sense of wonder, and awe.

Two Iowa Teens Charged with Murder of High School Spanish Teacher Nohema Graber

DES MOINES, Iowa – Two 16-year-old Iowa teens, Willard Noble Chaiden Miller and Jeremy Everett Goodale, have been charged with first-degree murder in the death of Fairfield High School Spanish teacher Nohema Graber. Graber's body was discovered in Chautauqua Park under a tarp, wheelbarrow, and railroad ties, suffering inflicted trauma to the head.

According to Jefferson County Attorney Chauncey Moulding, the suspects will be charged as adults due to the circumstances and their ages. "This was a brutal and senseless act of violence that has shaken our community to its core," Moulding said in a statement. "We will do everything in our power to ensure that justice is served."

Graber, 66, was remembered by the community as a leader and deeply loving towards her family, students, and friends. "Nohema was an incredible teacher and mentor to so many students," said Edith Cabrera, a friend of Graber's. "She had a heart of gold and will be deeply missed."

The Fairfield Community School District canceled classes following the incident, underscoring the community's shock and grief. "Our top priority is the well-being of our students and staff," said Laurie Noll, superintendent of the Fairfield Community School District. "We will do everything we can to support them through this difficult time."

The President of the Iowa State Education Association, Mike Beranek, expressed condolences and highlighted the role of educators in protecting students. "As educators, we are deeply saddened by this senseless act of violence," Beranek said in a statement. "We will continue to work towards creating safe and supportive learning environments for all students."

The community has expressed deep shock and grief at the news of Graber's death, struggling to understand the motivations behind the violent act. "This is a senseless tragedy that has left our community reeling," said Moulding. "We will continue to work with law enforcement to uncover the truth behind this heinous crime."

The investigation into Graber's death is ongoing, with social media activity and a search of the suspects' homes aiding the police investigation. "We are working tirelessly to gather evidence and bring those responsible to justice," said Moulding.

As the community mourns the loss of Graber, they are also working to support her family and loved ones during this difficult time. "Nohema was more than just a teacher – she was a beloved member of our community," said Cabrera. "We will do everything we can to honor her memory and ensure that her legacy lives on."

Luke walked for fifteen minutes, revolving in his mind various plans for the benefit of his friend Jim.

He was not aware that he was followed, nor, indeed, did he give much thought to the matter. He was too much engrossed in his plans for Jim's benefit.

Suddenly, however, he was recalled to himself by a rough voice saying:

"Hold on there a minute, mister."

The tone was not to be mistaken for politeness. Luke stopped short, and turned to confront the speaker.

He was a boy of seventeen, raggedly dressed, and having in his face a look that was both bold and sinister. By his side stood a younger boy, who kept partly behind him as if for protection.

"What do you want?" asked Luke, not feeling quite comfortable, though he was a boy of considerable courage.

"I want that five-dollar bill you're got," said the older boy, insolently.

Luke could not help starting. How did the boy know that he had a five-dollar bill? He had received it that very afternoon from his employer, Mr. Crawford.

"I don't know what you mean," said Luke. "I haven't got any five-dollar bill."

"You're a liar!" said the older boy, boldly. "I saw you get it changed at the grocer's."

Luke saw it was useless to deny the truth. He mentally cursed his folly in changing the bill. Had he kept it as it was, he might have escaped being robbed.

"Well, suppose I have," said Luke. "What business is that of yours?"

"You'd better shell out that bill, or it'll be the worse for you," said the older boy, menacingly. "Come, I mean business. We haven't any time to waste."

The younger boy, who had not yet spoken, here edged up to his companion, and whispered something in his ear.

The elder scowled.

"What difference does it make?" he said, roughly. "He's got the money, and we're going to have it."

Luke's heart beat fast. He began to fear that the ruffians would carry out their threat. What could he do? There was no one in sight to whom he could appeal for assistance.

Suddenly his eye fell upon the younger of his assailants. Where had he seen that boy before? He studied his face attentively.

"Tom Brooks, is that you?" he asked, abruptly.

The boy thus addressed started and looked confused. He evidently recognized Luke, but did not reply.

"Answer me," said Luke, "isn't your name Tom Brooks?"

"Yes, it is," muttered the boy. "But you'd better mind your own business."

"What are you doing with such company, Tom?" asked Luke, earnestly.

"That's my business, not yours," said Tom, sullenly. "Come along, Bill, let's go. I don't like this fellow."

The other boy hesitated. He looked from Luke to his companion, and back again.

"I'm going to have that five-dollar bill," he said, doggedly.

"No, you're not, Bill," said Luke, firmly. "Tom Brooks is not going to stand by and see me robbed."

"He's not, ain't he?" retorted Bill, sneeringly. "We'll see about that."

He took a step forward, but Tom Brooks threw himself in his way.

"No, Bill, you're not going to touch him," he said, resolutely.

"Get out of my way!" exclaimed Bill, angrily, trying to push Tom aside. "If you interfere, I'll give you a thrashing."

Tom stood his ground manfully. Though smaller than his companion, his courage was fully as great.

"I told you I wouldn't stand by and see him robbed," he repeated. "You'd better let him alone, Bill."

"We'll see if I don't get that bill," said Bill, turning upon his heel. "Come along."

With a last threatening look at Luke, he walked rapidly away, followed by Tom Brooks, who could not conceal the shame and confusion he felt at being detected in such company.

Waverly Braces for Another Round of Rain as Residents Continue to Recover from Devastating Floods

As Tropical Storm Ida bears down on Tennessee, the town of Waverly is bracing for another round of heavy rain, just as residents are still recovering from the devastating floods that killed 20 and damaged hundreds of homes. Melissa "Kay" Anderson, a local resident, said, "It's been a tough few weeks for us here in Waverly. The flooding was horrific, and now we're facing another round of rain. It's just one thing after another."

According to National Weather Service meteorologist John Cohen, Hurricane Ida has been downgraded to a tropical storm but is expected to bring 2 to 5 inches of rain to the area. "Ida will weaken into a depression as it moves inland, but it will still bring significant rain to the region," Cohen said. Waverly is currently under a flash flood watch, with continuous rain expected for 24 hours starting late Monday.

Residents are emotionally and physically preparing for the impact of the rain on their recovering homes and town. Over 800 truckloads of debris have been cleared by volunteer agencies, the National Guard, and the Tennessee Department of Transportation. Grey Collier, spokesperson for the Humphreys County Emergency Management Agency, said, "We're doing everything we can to prevent creek blockage and avoid further flooding. We're working closely with local residents and businesses to make sure everyone is prepared."

The town's Emergency Management Agency is also working to prevent creek blockage to avoid further flooding. Waverly Police Department is monitoring the situation and prepared for possible evacuations, though none are expected. Residents are encouraged to cover their homes and belongings with tarps available at a local staging area. ISIS-K: A Persistent Threat Post-Kabul Airport Tragedy

CNN – The bombing at Kabul airport in August, which resulted in the tragic loss of 13 US troops and over 90 Afghans, placed the spotlight on one of the region's most feared terror groups: ISIS-Khorasan, or ISIS-K. The ISIS affiliate, notorious for its ruthless tactics and extremist ideology, quickly claimed responsibility for the attack, showcasing its reach and determination to strike against both Western and Afghan targets.

In response to the Kabul airport bombing, US President Joe Biden vowed to hunt down those responsible, emphasizing that retribution would be swift and forceful. The attack marked ISIS-K's most significant action on the global stage, attracting widespread condemnation and renewing focus on the group's capacities and objectives.

Established in 2015, ISIS-K rapidly gained a reputation for its lethal attacks across Afghanistan and parts of Pakistan. By 2018, the group was ranked the world's fourth deadliest terror organization, a testament to its brutal campaign that has claimed thousands of lives. Operating mostly in Central Asia, ISIS-K's strength is currently estimated to be between 1,500 and 2,000 members, a sizeable force capable of mounting significant terrorist operations.

The genesis of ISIS-K traces back to Pakistani militants, drawing also recruits from Taliban defectors and seasoned jihadists. These diverse origins have forged a coalition united by a radical interpretation of Islam, with aspirations far beyond the borders of Afghanistan and Pakistan. Chief among ISIS-K's goals is the establishment of a caliphate governed strictly by sharia law, a vision that starkly contrasts with the Taliban's own rule in Afghanistan.

Despite a bitter rivalry with the Taliban, whom they view as adversaries rather than allies, ISIS-K has maintained a relentless assault on Afghanistan's civilian population. The group has been responsible for some of the most heinous attacks in recent years, ranging from suicide bombings to targeted assaults on minority communities, aiming to sow discord and instability.

Despite suffering setbacks, including a series of targeted strikes by US and Afghan forces which have degraded its capabilities, ISIS-K remains a formidable threat. The group has demonstrated remarkable resilience, adapting to changing circumstances and even managing to infiltrate urban areas with potential sleeper cells poised to strike.

The concerted efforts by US and Afghan military forces have indeed curtailed ISIS-K's operational capacity to some extent. High-profile leaders have been eliminated in raids, and their territorial control has been challenged. However, the threat posed by ISIS-K has not been extinguished; the group's ideology continues to inspire militants, and its cells are suspected of plotting further attacks, including against US personnel and interests.

The Kabul airport attack serves as a harrowing reminder of ISIS-K's capabilities and the group's intent to pursue its agenda irrespective of the costs. The loss of American and Afghan lives in such a callous act of terrorism has galvanized international resolve against ISIS-K, leading to increased cooperation between nations in the counterterrorism arena.

Facing the dual threats of ISIS-K and the Taliban's resurgence, Afghanistan finds itself at a critical juncture. The international community's withdrawal from the country has left a vacuum that these groups are eager to exploit, raising concerns about the future stability of the region.

As ISIS-K continues to pose a clear and present danger, the need for a comprehensive strategy to combat its influence is more pressing than ever. The group's ability to carry out high-profile attacks underscores the complexity of Afghanistan's security landscape and the international challenge of rooting out extremism.

Looking ahead, the fight against ISIS-K will require a multifaceted approach, combining military action with efforts to undermine the group's ideological appeal and financial networks. The international community must remain vigilant, supporting Afghan forces and investing in sustainable solutions to counter radicalization and prevent future tragedies like the Kabul airport bombing.

In the shadow of the Kabul tragedy, the persistence of ISIS-K serves as a stark reminder of the enduring threat of terrorism. As the world grapples with this ongoing challenge, the memory of those lost in the attack reinforces the resolve to combat extremism in all its forms.

Together We Will Overcome: My Commitment to Ending the COVID-19 Pandemic

Ladies and gentlemen, esteemed guests, and fellow Americans, I stand before you today with a heavy heart and a resolute spirit. Our nation has faced an unprecedented challenge in the form of the COVID-19 pandemic, and together, we have made great strides in the battle against this invisible enemy. But as we have seen with the emergence of the Delta variant, our work is far from over.

I addressed the nation last week to share the latest developments in our fight against COVID-19 and to outline a new plan to combat this virus and protect the health and safety of the American people. I want to speak to you today not just as your President, but as a fellow citizen who shares in your concerns and your hopes for a brighter future.

The Delta variant has brought renewed urgency to our efforts to vaccinate as many Americans as possible. It is important to remember that the vaccines are our best defense against this virus. They have been shown to be safe and effective, and they are our ticket back to normalcy. But too many Americans remain unvaccinated, leaving our communities vulnerable to outbreaks and the devastating consequences that come with them.

That's why I am announcing a new plan to combat COVID-19, a plan that focuses on vaccination mandates for larger employers, increased testing, and school safety measures. I believe that this comprehensive approach is the key to putting an end to this pandemic once and for all.

One of the most significant components of this plan is the requirement for employers with 100 or more employees to ensure their workforce is fully vaccinated or tested weekly. Major companies like United Airlines, Disney, Tyson Foods, and Fox News have already announced that they will be implementing vaccination requirements, and I believe that this trend will continue as more businesses realize the importance of protecting their employees and their customers.

Another crucial aspect of this plan is the federal government's commitment to requiring vaccinations for all workers in healthcare facilities that receive Medicare or Medicaid funding. This will impact 17 million healthcare workers and will go a long way in ensuring the safety of our most vulnerable populations.

In addition to these measures, I will be signing executive orders mandating vaccinations for all federal employees and contractors who do business with the federal government. I believe that it is the responsibility of the federal government to lead by example and to do everything in its power to protect the health and safety of its workforce and the American people.

But this plan is not just about mandates and requirements. It is also about keeping our schools safe and open. I am calling on governors to require vaccinations for all teachers and staff, and I am committed to providing the resources and support necessary to make this a reality. The safety and well-being of our children should be our top priority, and we cannot afford to let politics stand in the way of that goal.

Another important component of this plan is an emphasis on increasing testing and making it more accessible and affordable. I understand that testing has been a challenge for many Americans, and I am committed to using every tool at my disposal to address this issue. That's why I will be using the Defense Production Act to boost production of rapid tests, making them more widely available to those who need them.

My plan also seeks to protect the economic recovery by expanding the COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loan program for small businesses. I know that many small businesses have been hit hard by this pandemic, and I am committed to doing everything in my power to help them get back on their feet.

Finally, efforts will continue to improve care for those with COVID-19, including increasing the distribution of monoclonal antibody treatments and ensuring equity in vaccine distribution. We cannot afford to leave anyone behind in our efforts to end this pandemic, and I am committed to ensuring that every American has access to the resources and care they need.

In conclusion, I want to reiterate my commitment to ending this pandemic and to working with you, the American people, to build a better, stronger, and more resilient nation. Together, we have faced challenges before, and together, we will overcome this one. We will get through this, and we will come out on the other side stronger and more united than ever before.

Thank you, and may God bless you all, and may God bless the United States of America.
